properties.decision:
Answers option (b) of dec:idea-backlog-belongs-in-the-graph WITHOUT adding a node type, which was that option's strongest objection.

THE MECHANISM. A defect found by use is recorded as a `TemporalFact`: `subject_id` = the node it indicts, `fact_type` = "defect", `statement` = the claim (FULLTEXT-INDEXED, so search_design finds it), `value` = JSON carrying the measurement, `basis` = "measured" (never "forecast" — a defect is observed), `confidence` = how sure the observer is. Edges: HAS_TEMPORAL_FACT from the indicted node, ABOUT_ENTITY back to it, VALID_FROM the epoch it was observed. VALID_TO is set WHEN IT IS FIXED — absent means still true.

WHY THIS TYPE AND NOT A NEW ONE. Four reasons, each checked rather than assumed. (1) TemporalFact's own extraction_hint already says "a time-bounded assertion true only between two epochs", and a defect is exactly that: true of the build from the epoch it was found until the epoch it was fixed. (2) `fact_type` is `{ type: string, indexed: true }` — free-form and INDEXED, not an enum, so "defect" needs no schema change. (3) THERE IS A SHIPPING PRECEDENT for using fact_type as a discriminator a reader queries: crates/reflow2-core/src/readiness.rs:57 marks readiness assertions this way and reads them back. This is not a new convention, it is an existing one applied to a second case. (4) The prior against new vocabulary is heavy and documented — this project proposed and WITHDREW two node types in one week (Attestation to TemporalFact, Hazard to DesignRule + CONSTRAINS) — and dec:idea-backlog-belongs-in-the-graph itself flagged TemporalFact as probably already the shape.

WHAT THIS FIXES, precisely. The graph had no way to say "this capability is BUILT, VERIFIED, and does not do what it claims". Verification answers whether a check PASSES, and every defect of this kind sat under a passing check. DriftEvent answers whether code moved away from the design, and in these cases code and design AGREED and both were wrong. HEAL's issues are computed from graph shape and vanish between runs. So the largest category of backlog row had nowhere to go, which is why it went to markdown.

THE LIFECYCLE IS THE PART MARKDOWN DID BY HAND. A row today is annotated "DONE 2026-08-05" in prose. Here, fixing a defect means setting VALID_TO to the epoch that fixed it, so "is this still broken?" is a graph question rather than a reading-comprehension one — and the history survives instead of being overwritten.

MEASURED STARTING POINT: reflow2's own graph contained ZERO TemporalFacts before this decision, despite BL-68 building the measured/forecast distinction for them. The type was built, correct, and unused.

WHAT IS STILL OWED, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS. Nothing in the LOOP reads these yet. `statement` is fulltext so search_design finds them today — genuinely better than grepping a 592 KB file, and the reason this is worth doing before the reader exists — but loop_status does not count open defects, and until it does, a defect recorded here is discoverable rather than SURFACED. That reader is the next increment and it is a Rust change. Recorded so the gap is on the record rather than discovered later: writing facts nothing reads is this project's own recurring declared-and-read-by-nothing failure, and doing it knowingly with the reader scheduled is different from doing it by accident.

NOT CLAIMED: that this retires docs/backlog.md. Three of the four backlog categories already had homes (unbuilt work is a planned Capability, an open question is a proposed Decision, a discovered limit is a Constraint or DesignRule) and were not being used either. This decision closes the one category that had NO home. Deriving the markdown from the graph is option (d) and remains open.
properties.name: A defect found by USING a built capability is a TemporalFact with fact_type "defect" — no new vocabulary, and the lifecycle comes free
properties.rationale: Chosen rather than left open because dec:idea-backlog-belongs-in-the-graph has held five options and no choice since 2026-08-04, and the cost of that is measured: 218 backlog rows, 592 KB, and an accepted decision (dec:export-once-per-pr) violated and re-derived for the third time in the very session that asked for the fix. Anthony called it embarrassing and asked for it as first priority; the conservative option — reuse an existing type with an existing reader precedent — is the one that can ship now. Left `proposed` with him as approver rather than accepted: dec:three-party-checks says the human decides, and this changes how the project records its own learning.
